policy: Each seed food maps to one FDC food in the state the seed and its recipes use: raw unless the seed names a state, canned legumes drained, grains, pasta and dry legumes dry.

Foundation Foods is preferred. SR Legacy is used when Foundation has no matching food, or when the Foundation record lacks a nutrient the planner scores that SR has: energy, protein, fat, carbohydrate, sodium and potassium, fibre for plant foods, and saturated fat when total fat is 1 g or more.
A matching state outweighs completeness: black-beans-canned keeps Foundation without saturated fat because SR has no drained black beans.
When Foundation splits a generic seed food into cultivars, the clear market default is used (yellow onion, navel orange); otherwise SR's generic food is (apple, tomato).
Where enriched and unenriched grain products both exist, unenriched is used: enrichment is a US practice, so iron and B vitamins are a floor rather than a ceiling.
description is FDC's own description; Tools/import-fdc.py fails when it does not match the data, so a mistyped fdcId cannot pass.
A food with no defensible match has no dataset and keeps its seedApproximate values; unmatched gives the reason.
portions and densityGPerMl, when present, replace the seed's values; portionNote says why. Use them only for a gram weight FDC shows to be wrong.
